description: Canonical redaction taxonomy. One source, consumed by scripts/redact.py, lib/redact.js, the memory write path, and the generated release/document skill docs. Calibration rule: a gate that cries wolf gets ignored, so only genuinely-secret credentials are HIGH.

tiers.HIGH: Genuinely-secret credential. BLOCKS the write or the send. There is intentionally no per-pattern key to disable HIGH blocking.
tiers.MEDIUM: PII, legal or damaging content, internal-leak, or a credential shape with a high false-positive rate. CONFIRMS with the user.
tiers.LOW: Surfaced only. No prompt, no block.

visibilityRule: Repository visibility never promotes a tier. A public repo earns sterner per-finding confirmation on MEDIUM findings; it does not turn MEDIUM into HIGH. Auto-promotion is how a gate becomes noise, and noise is how a gate gets switched off.
redosRule: Every regex must be linear-time. No nested unbounded quantifiers. `python scripts/redact.py --lint` fails CI on a catastrophic form.

patterns.description: AWS secret key, proximity-gated so ordinary base64 does not trip it
Bearer token in a literal header
Stripe publishable key. Public by design, but routinely pasted alongside the secret one.
Google API key. Frequently domain-restricted; context decides.
JWT. Often an expired sample in a test fixture.
Absolute Windows user path. Leaks a developer's username into shared memory that syncs organization-wide.
A note that a credential needs rotating

suppressions.description: Scoped to the matched span, not the line. A real key on the same line as the word 'example' still counts.
Test fixture paths suppress MEDIUM and LOW only. A HIGH-tier credential in a test file is still a HIGH-tier credential — that is where they most often get committed.

memory.shared.write.why: memory/shared/ syncs to every connected repo. A captured credential is an organization-wide replication event, not a local mistake.

memory.decision.write.why: The decision log is re-injected into future prompts, which makes it both a storage surface and an injection surface.

context.file.write.why: orchestrator-context.md is committed in some repos and is the densest artifact in the system.

release.artifact.write.why: Release notes and CHANGELOG entries are published.

chat.stream.why: Blocking the user's primary interaction over a scan is a worse outcome than a warning (P5).

hub.clone.why: Pulls executable content — SKILL.md files that steer agents.
